4. If the reading exceeds the standard, adjust it to align with the industry standard.
5. Consider factors such as wind direction during the monitoring period and the proximity of the monitoring station to ensure credibility.
6. If wind direction on the day was from an industry source, reduce pollutant concentration readings from that day.
7. If the monitoring station was near a dense residential area, reduce pollutant concentration readings from that day to align with the industry standard.
8. Compile the adjusted data into a falsified report.
